A long-stroke six: heavy slow pulses (16 Hz), a lumpy carburettor idle, a race gear set that sings a little (0.4), live-axle lash. The in-game name is just Chevrolet Opala (roster); the 1979 and 1986 Stock Cars are separate entries. Nothing electronic (wiki).

ams2:Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1979.name: Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1979
ams2:Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1979.notes: First-season Stock Car Brasil (1979): near-stock Opala 4.1 six at 176 hp (wiki), 4-speed H-pattern, 1100 kg. Lazy big six, lots of flywheel. The wiki infobox writes the name Chevrolet Opala (1979); the roster writes Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1979: confirm which string the sim sends. Nothing electronic (wiki).

ams2:Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1986.name: Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1986
ams2:Chevrolet Opala Stock Cars 1986.notes: 1986 Stock Car Opala: the 4.1 six at 248 hp (wiki), 4-speed H-pattern, 1080 kg. Nothing electronic (wiki).

ams2:Chevrolet Omega Stock Car 1999.name: Chevrolet Omega Stock Car 1999
ams2:Chevrolet Omega Stock Car 1999.notes: 1999 Stock Car Omega: the Opala 4.1 six at 338 hp (wiki) in a tube-frame silhouette, 5-speed dogleg H-pattern, 1080 kg. Nothing electronic (wiki).

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2019.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2019
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2019.notes: Stock Car Brasil 2019: Mast JLR 5.7 cross-plane V8 at 473 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential on paddles, 1340 kg, push-to-pass. Big V8 lope and heavy pulses (16 Hz), a straight-cut sequential (whine 0.8). The wiki infobox writes Chevrolet Cruze (2019); confirm the string. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2020.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2020
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2020.notes: Stock Car Brasil 2020 Cruze: same V8 and sequential as 2019. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2020.name: Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2020
ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2020.notes: Stock Car Brasil 2020 Corolla: the series' spec V8 and sequential under a Toyota shell. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2021.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2021
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2021.notes: Stock Car Brasil 2021 Cruze: spec V8 and sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2021.name: Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2021
ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2021.notes: Stock Car Brasil 2021 Corolla: spec V8 and sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2022.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2022
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2022.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2022 Cruze: spec V8 and sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2022.name: Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2022
ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2022.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2022 Corolla: spec V8 and sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2023.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2023
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2023.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2023: the wiki lists a 6.8 litre V8 at 353 kW for this season (the series moved to a larger-displacement spec engine), 6-speed sequential paddles, 1370 kg, push-to-pass. Heavier pulses still (carrier 15 Hz). Wiki infobox name Chevrolet Cruze (2023): confirm. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2023.name: Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2023
ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2023.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2023 Corolla: the 2023 spec V8. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2024.name: Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2024
ams2:Chevrolet Cruze Stock Car 2024.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2024 Cruze: the 2023 spec V8 carried over. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2024.name: Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2024
ams2:Toyota Corolla Stock Car 2024.notes: Stock Car Pro Series 2024 Corolla: the 2023 spec V8 carried over. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Stock USA Gen1.name: Stock USA Gen1
ams2:Stock USA Gen1.notes: NASCAR-style Gen 1 (1990s body): 358 cubic inch pushrod V8 on a carburettor, about 750 hp, 9000 rpm, 4-speed H-pattern with straight-cut gears (whine 0.5), solid rear axle with lots of lash. The lumpiest big V8 in the game (rock 0.9, thump 1.0 at 15 Hz). No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Stock USA Gen2.name: Stock USA Gen2
ams2:Stock USA Gen2.notes: NASCAR-style Gen 2 (2000s body): same 358 V8 with fuel injection from 2012 on, 4-speed H-pattern. Values as Gen1. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Stock USA Gen3.name: Stock USA Gen3
ams2:Stock USA Gen3.notes: NASCAR Next Gen style: 5.86 litre V8 at 677 hp (wiki, the restricted figure), 5-speed sequential, independent rear, 1542 kg. Sequential straight-cut box (whine 0.7). No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Stock USA Gen3 LM.name: Stock USA Gen3 LM
ams2:Stock USA Gen3 LM.notes: The Garage 56 Le Mans version of the Next Gen car: same V8 and sequential, more power, endurance lights. Values as Gen3. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Super V8.name: Super V8
ams2:Super V8.notes: Australian Supercars Gen2 ZB style: 5.0 V8 at 631 hp (wiki), 7500 rpm, 6-speed sequential stick, 1395 kg. Cross-plane lope with a famous crackling overrun (pops 0.8), straight-cut Albins sequential (whine 0.8). Roster name Super V8 (Gen2 ZB); the wiki page is Super V8: confirm the string. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Judd.name: Metalmoro AJR Judd
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Judd.notes: Brazilian P1 prototype with the Judd 4.2 V10 at 556 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 950 kg: a screaming NA V10 in a 950 kg car, straight-cut sequential. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Nissan.name: Metalmoro AJR Nissan
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Nissan.notes: AJR with the Nissan 3.5 V6 turbo at 560 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential, 960 kg: turbo V6 with a big dump on lift. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Honda.name: Metalmoro AJR Honda
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Honda.notes: AJR with the Honda 2.4 four turbo at 579 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 935 kg: a big turbo four, more shake and a bigger dump. TC yes, ABS yes (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Chevrolet.name: Metalmoro AJR Chevrolet
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Chevrolet.notes: AJR with the 6.2 LS V8 at 594 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 960 kg: cross-plane rumble and heavy pulses. TC yes, ABS yes (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Chevrolet.name: Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Chevrolet
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Chevrolet.notes: The Gen2 AJR chassis with the 6.2 LS V8. Values as the Gen1 Chevrolet. TC and ABS on.

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Honda.name: Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Honda
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Honda.notes: The Gen2 AJR with the Honda 2.4 turbo four. Values as the Gen1 Honda. TC and ABS on.

ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Nissan.name: Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Nissan
ams2:Metalmoro AJR Gen2 Nissan.notes: The Gen2 AJR with the Nissan 3.5 V6 turbo; the Gen2 cars carry the class electronics, so TC and ABS on (the Gen1 Nissan has neither per the wiki).

ams2:Ginetta G58.name: Ginetta G58
ams2:Ginetta G58.notes: Ginetta G58 prototype with the 6.2 LS V8 at 564 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential, 1020 kg. TC yes, ABS yes (wiki).

ams2:Ginetta G58 Gen2.name: Ginetta G58 Gen2
ams2:Ginetta G58 Gen2.notes: The updated G58 for P1 Gen 2: same V8 and sequential. TC and ABS on.

ams2:Ligier JS P320.name: Ligier JS P320
ams2:Ligier JS P320.notes: LMP3 Gen 2: Nissan VK56 5.6 V8 at 455 hp, 6-speed sequential paddles. A production-based cross-plane V8 with a race exhaust. LMP3 allows traction control, no ABS.

ams2:Sigma P1 G5.name: Sigma P1 G5
ams2:Sigma P1 G5.notes: Sigma P1 G5: 6.9 litre NA V8 at 573 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 1050 kg. The biggest-displacement V8 here, slow heavy pulses. TC yes, ABS yes (wiki).

ams2:Sigma P1.name: Sigma P1
ams2:Sigma P1.notes: P2-class Sigma P1: 4.2 V8 turbo at 501 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential, 1170 kg. Turbo V8 dump on lift. TC yes, ABS yes (wiki).

ams2:MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P2.name: MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P2
ams2:MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P2.notes: MRX with the Duratec 2.0 turbo at 372 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential, 800 kg. TC yes, ABS no (wiki).

ams2:Metalmoro MRX Honda P3.name: Metalmoro MRX Honda P3
ams2:Metalmoro MRX Honda P3.notes: MRX with the Honda K20 2.0 NA at 303 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential stick, 740 kg: a high-revving NA four (9000 rpm) with overrun crackle. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3.name: MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3
ams2:MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3.notes: MRX with the NA Duratec 2.0 in P3 trim (about 280 hp), 6-speed sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Metalmoro MRX Duratec P4.name: Metalmoro MRX Duratec P4
ams2:Metalmoro MRX Duratec P4.notes: MRX with the Duratec 2.0 in P4 trim (about 230 hp), 6-speed sequential. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Roco 001.name: Roco 001
ams2:Roco 001.notes: Roco 001 P3 prototype: 1.5 four at 283 hp (wiki) in 550 kg, which means a very high-revving motorcycle-derived engine, 6-speed sequential: buzz, no inertia, high cut. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:MCR S2000.name: MCR S2000
ams2:MCR S2000.notes: MCR S2000 P4 prototype: 2.0 NA four at 217 hp (wiki), 5-speed sequential, 525 kg. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Puma P052.name: Puma P052
ams2:Puma P052.notes: GT5-class Puma P052: mid-engined 1.6 turbo four at 163 hp (wiki), 5-speed H-pattern, 940 kg. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Ginetta G40.name: Ginetta G40
ams2:Ginetta G40.notes: GT5-class Ginetta G40: Ford 1.8 Zetec four at about 175 hp, 5-speed sequential dog box (whine 0.7), 800 kg. The G40 Cup is a separate entry (wiki infobox name Ginetta G40 Cup). No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Ginetta G40 Cup.name: Ginetta G40 Cup
ams2:Ginetta G40 Cup.notes: Ginetta Junior / G40 Cup car: 1.8 Ford Zetec at 142 hp (wiki), 5-speed H-pattern manual (synchro shape, clutch 1.0), 925 kg. The novice car: soft, lots of lug. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Ginetta G55 GT4 Supercup.name: Ginetta G55 GT4 Supercup
ams2:Ginetta G55 GT4 Supercup.notes: G55 Supercup: Ford 3.7 Cyclone V6 at 370 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 1195 kg. Supercup runs without aids: no TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Ginetta G55 GT4.name: Ginetta G55 GT4
ams2:Ginetta G55 GT4.notes: G55 in GT4 trim: the 3.7 V6 at about 350 hp with the GT4 electronics. ABS and TC on.

ams2:Ginetta G55 GT3.name: Ginetta G55 GT3
ams2:Ginetta G55 GT3.notes: G55 GT3: 4.3 V8 (Ford-based) at about 440 hp, 6-speed sequential dog box. GT3-style: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Ultima GTR Race.name: Ultima GTR Race
ams2:Ultima GTR Race.notes: GT Open Ultima GTR race car: 6.2 LS V8 around 560 hp in a 1000 kg kit-car chassis, sequential dog box. GT Open spec without aids: no TC, no ABS.

ams2:Ligier JS2 R.name: Ligier JS2 R
ams2:Ligier JS2 R.notes: Ligier European Series JS2 R: Ford 3.7 V6 at 330 hp, 6-speed sequential paddles. The JS2 R runs ABS and TC.

ams2:Ligier JS P4.name: Ligier JS P4
ams2:Ligier JS P4.notes: Ligier JS P4 prototype: the same 3.7 V6 at about 330 hp, 6-speed sequential. TC on, no ABS (the P4 class runs without it).

ams2:Ligier JS P217.name: Ligier JS P217
ams2:Ligier JS P217.notes: LMP2 Gen 2: Gibson GK428 4.2 V8 at 600 hp, 8500 rpm, Xtrac 6-speed sequential paddles. A flat-plane race V8 with a loud overrun. LMP2 runs traction control, no ABS.

ams2:Oreca 07.name: Oreca 07
ams2:Oreca 07.notes: LMP2 Gen 2 Oreca 07: the same Gibson V8 and Xtrac box. TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Cadillac DPi-V.R.name: Cadillac DPi-V.R
ams2:Cadillac DPi-V.R.notes: IMSA DPi: ECR 5.5 cross-plane V8 at about 600 hp, 7600 rpm, Xtrac 6-speed sequential paddles. The big V8 rumble in a prototype, loud overrun. DPi: TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Kartcross.name: Kartcross
ams2:Kartcross.notes: Kartcross buggy: a 1.0 litre motorcycle inline-four (about 150 hp, 13000 rpm) with the bike's 6-speed sequential dog box and a chain drive, in a 400 kg tube frame: all buzz, no inertia, lots of shunt. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT3.name: Audi R8 LMS GT3
ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT3.notes: First-generation R8 LMS GT3 (2015 car): 5.2 NA V10 about 560 hp, X-trac six-speed sequential dog box (whine 0.8), loud overrun. Same values as the AC R8 LMS. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:BMW M6 GT3.name: BMW M6 GT3
ams2:BMW M6 GT3.notes: S63 4.4 twin-turbo cross-plane V8 at about 580 hp: a rumbling turbo V8 with a big dump on lift (1.6) and a crackle, torque into the lash (shunt 0.75). Ricardo six-speed sequential. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren 720S GT3.name: McLaren 720S GT3
ams2:McLaren 720S GT3.notes: The 720S GT3 (roster name just McLaren 720S): M840T 4.0 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 at about 520 hp, Ricardo six-speed sequential. Flat-plane buzz, turbo flutter and dump. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT3.name: Mercedes-AMG GT3
ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT3.notes: M159 6.2 NA cross-plane V8, side exhausts, the loudest overrun bark in GT3 (pops 0.8), lumpy race idle. Hewland six-speed sequential. Same values as the AC AMG GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3.name: Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3
ams2:Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3.notes: VR38DETT 3.8 twin-turbo V6 at about 550 hp, rear-drive, Ricardo sequential. Same values as the AC GT-R GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 R.name: Porsche 911 GT3 R
ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 R.notes: 991.2 GT3 R: 4.0 NA flat-six at about 500 hp, 9000 rpm, six-speed sequential dog box (whine 0.9), race exhaust (pops 0.8). Same values as the AC GT3 R 2016. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO.name: Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO
ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO.notes: GT3 Gen 2 Vantage: the AMG-sourced 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8 at about 535 hp, Xtrac six-speed sequential: turbo V8 rumble, dump on lift. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II.name: Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II
ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II.notes: The 2022 evo II: same 5.2 V10 and sequential as the first-generation car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:BMW M4 GT3.name: BMW M4 GT3
ams2:BMW M4 GT3.notes: P58 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six at about 590 hp: a smooth six with two turbos that breathe hard on lift (1.6) and a cracking race exhaust. Xtrac six-speed sequential. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R.name: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R.notes: LT6-based 5.5 flat-plane V8 at about 500 hp restricted, 8600 rpm: unlike every other Corvette here it is a flat-plane crank, so it screams rather than rumbles (buzz 0.95). Xtrac six-speed sequential. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2.name: Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2
ams2:Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2.notes: EVO2 Huracán GT3: the 5.2 V10 and X-trac sequential, the Audi's twin. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren 720S GT3 EVO.name: McLaren 720S GT3 EVO
ams2:McLaren 720S GT3 EVO.notes: The 2023 EVO: same M840T twin-turbo V8 and Ricardo sequential as the 720S GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO.name: Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO
ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO.notes: The 2020 EVO: same 6.2 V8 and Hewland box as the AMG GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Porsche 992 GT3-R.name: Porsche 992 GT3-R
ams2:Porsche 992 GT3-R.notes: 992 GT3 R: the flat-six grown to 4.2 litres, about 565 hp, 9250 rpm, six-speed sequential (whine 0.9). GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Alpine A110 GT4 EVO.name: Alpine A110 GT4 EVO
ams2:Alpine A110 GT4 EVO.notes: 1.8 turbo four at about 300 hp in a light mid-engined GT4, turbo whoosh on lift (1.5), six-speed sequential. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GT4 EVO.name: Aston Martin Vantage GT4 EVO
ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GT4 EVO.notes: The 4.0 twin-turbo AMG V8 in GT4 tune (about 450 hp), Xtrac sequential: turbo V8 rumble. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT4.name: Audi R8 LMS GT4
ams2:Audi R8 LMS GT4.notes: GT4 R8: the road car's 5.2 V10 at about 495 hp with the seven-speed S tronic DCT (synchro-shaped shifts). GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:BMW M4 GT4.name: BMW M4 GT4
ams2:BMW M4 GT4.notes: G82 M4 GT4: S58 3.0 twin-turbo six at about 550 hp with the ZF eight-speed automatic (synchro-shaped shifts). GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Chevrolet Camaro GT4.R.name: Chevrolet Camaro GT4.R
ams2:Chevrolet Camaro GT4.R.notes: LT1 6.2 pushrod V8 at about 480 hp: the muscle-car lope in a GT4, Xtrac six-speed sequential. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren 570S GT4.name: McLaren 570S GT4
ams2:McLaren 570S GT4.notes: The 570S GT4 (roster name McLaren 570S): 3.8 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 restricted to about 450 hp, seven-speed DCT. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT4.name: Mercedes-AMG GT4
ams2:Mercedes-AMG GT4.notes: M178 4.0 twin-turbo V8 at about 480 hp with the AMG seven-speed DCT transaxle: turbo V8 rumble, DCT shifts. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR.name: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR
ams2:Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR.notes: The 981 Clubsport MR: 3.8 flat-six at 385 hp with the PDK (synchro shape). Same values as the AC Clubsport. GT4: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GTE.name: Aston Martin Vantage GTE
ams2:Aston Martin Vantage GTE.notes: 2018 Vantage GTE: 4.0 twin-turbo V8 at about 500 hp, Xtrac six-speed sequential. Turbo V8 character. GTE: ABS and TC on.

ams2:BMW M8 GTE.name: BMW M8 GTE
ams2:BMW M8 GTE.notes: S63-based 4.0 twin-turbo V8 at about 500 hp, Xtrac sequential: the M6 GT3's engine family in the GTE car. GTE: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C8.R.name: Chevrolet Corvette C8.R
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C8.R.notes: C8.R: the 5.5 flat-plane LT6 race engine, about 500 hp, 8500 rpm, Xtrac sequential: a screaming Corvette, unlike the C7.R's cross-plane rumble. GTE: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Porsche 911 RSR-19.name: Porsche 911 RSR-19
ams2:Porsche 911 RSR-19.notes: 2019 RSR: mid-mounted 4.2 flat-six at about 510 hp, 9250 rpm, side exhausts, six-speed sequential. GTE: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren F1 GTR.name: McLaren F1 GTR
ams2:McLaren F1 GTR.notes: 1997 Longtail: BMW S70/2 6.1 V12 restricted to about 600 hp, 6-speed sequential dog box (the Longtail had the X-trac sequential). Same values as the AC F1 GTR. 1997 GT1: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Mercedes-Benz CLK LM.name: Mercedes-Benz CLK LM
ams2:Mercedes-Benz CLK LM.notes: 1998 CLK LM: M119 5.0 cross-plane V8 (the GTR's V12 replaced for Le Mans) at about 600 hp, X-trac six-speed sequential. 1998 GT1: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Nissan R390 GT1.name: Nissan R390 GT1
ams2:Nissan R390 GT1.notes: 1998 R390: VRH35L 3.5 twin-turbo V8 at about 650 hp, X-trac six-speed sequential. Two big turbos dumping on lift (1.7). 1998 GT1: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Porsche 911 GT1-98.name: Porsche 911 GT1-98
ams2:Porsche 911 GT1-98.notes: Same car as the AC 911 GT1-98: 3.2 twin-turbo flat-six, six-speed sequential. Values copied. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Aston Martin DBR9.name: Aston Martin DBR9
ams2:Aston Martin DBR9.notes: 2005 GT1: 6.0 V12 at about 600 hp restricted, 7000 rpm, Xtrac six-speed sequential, the howl of a big NA twelve. GT1 of 2005 allowed ABS and TC: both on.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C5-R.name: Chevrolet Corvette C5-R
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C5-R.notes: C5-R: 7.0 pushrod cross-plane V8 at about 610 hp, 6500 rpm, Xtrac six-speed sequential: the heaviest pulses of the GT1 field (15 Hz), a huge overrun bark. 2005 GT1: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Dodge Viper GTS-R.name: Dodge Viper GTS-R
ams2:Dodge Viper GTS-R.notes: 8.0 pushrod V10 at about 650 hp and only 6000 rpm: a truck-derived ten with an odd-fire lumpiness (rock 0.8, thump 1.0 at 15 Hz). Six-speed sequential. 2005 GT1 spec: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Lamborghini Murcielago R-GT.name: Lamborghini Murcielago R-GT
ams2:Lamborghini Murcielago R-GT.notes: Reiter-built R-GT: 6.0 V12 at about 580 hp restricted, rear-drive, Holinger six-speed sequential. 2005 GT1: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Lister Storm GTM.name: Lister Storm GTM
ams2:Lister Storm GTM.notes: Storm GTM: 7.0 Jaguar V12 (the XJR-9's engine) at about 600 hp, front-mounted, six-speed sequential: a lazier, heavier V12 than the Italian ones. 2005 GT1: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Maserati MC12 GT1.name: Maserati MC12 GT1
ams2:Maserati MC12 GT1.notes: Same car as the AC MC12 GT1. Values copied. ABS and TC on.

ams2:Milano GT55.name: Milano GT55
ams2:Milano GT55.notes: Fictional GT1 (wiki: Ferrari 550 GT1 inspired): 6.0 V12 at 576 hp, 6-speed sequential, 1235 kg. Front-engined V12 howl. Wiki: no TC, no ABS, which is how the Prodrive 550 ran.

ams2:Saleen S7-R GT1.name: Saleen S7-R GT1
ams2:Saleen S7-R GT1.notes: S7-R: 7.0 Ford-based pushrod V8 at about 600 hp, mid-mounted, six-speed sequential: big-block rumble behind your head. 2005 GT1: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Milano GT36.name: Milano GT36
ams2:Milano GT36.notes: Fictional GT2 (wiki: Ferrari 360 GT based): 3.6 flat-plane V8 at 471 hp, 6-speed sequential, 1185 kg. Wiki: no TC, no ABS.

ams2:Panoz Esperante GTLM.name: Panoz Esperante GTLM
ams2:Panoz Esperante GTLM.notes: Esperante GTLM: front-mounted Ford 5.0 pushrod-derived V8 (Elan) at about 450 hp, six-speed sequential, the 2006 Le Mans GT2 winner. 2005 GT2 spec in the game: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Porsche 996 GT3 RSR.name: Porsche 996 GT3 RSR
ams2:Porsche 996 GT3 RSR.notes: 996 GT3 RSR: 3.6 flat-six at about 445 hp, 8250 rpm, six-speed sequential dog box. 2005 GT2: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Spyker C8 Spyder GT2-R.name: Spyker C8 Spyder GT2-R
ams2:Spyker C8 Spyder GT2-R.notes: C8 Spyder GT2-R: Audi 3.8 (4.2-derived) V8 at about 400 hp, mid-mounted, six-speed sequential. 2005 GT2: ABS and TC on.

ams2:TVR Tuscan T400R GT2.name: TVR Tuscan T400R GT2
ams2:TVR Tuscan T400R GT2.notes: T400R: TVR's own 4.0 Speed Six inline-six at about 400 hp, front-mounted, a rough-edged straight six with a loud exhaust, sequential box. 2005 GT2: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.R.name: Chevrolet Corvette C3.R
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.R.notes: 1970s C3 race car: 7.0 big-block V8 on a Holley, about 600 hp, 6500 rpm, side pipes: the biggest lope and heaviest pulses in the game (14 Hz), 4-speed Muncie H-pattern with lots of lash. Nothing electronic.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.R Convertible.name: Chevrolet Corvette C3.R Convertible
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.R Convertible.notes: The open C3.R: identical mechanicals. Nothing electronic.

ams2:Porsche 911 RSR 74.name: Porsche 911 RSR 74
ams2:Porsche 911 RSR 74.notes: The GT Classic 911 RSR 3.0, the same car as the AC Carrera RSR 3.0. Values copied. Nothing electronic.

ams2:BMW M3 E46 GTR.name: BMW M3 E46 GTR
ams2:BMW M3 E46 GTR.notes: 2004 E46 GTR: P60 4.0 V8 at about 450 hp, 8000 rpm, six-speed sequential (the ALMS/Nürburgring car). No ABS, no TC in the game.

ams2:Gillet Vertigo Streiff.name: Gillet Vertigo Streiff
ams2:Gillet Vertigo Streiff.notes: Belgian Vertigo Streiff: Maserati-derived 4.2 V8 at about 420 hp in a 900 kg carbon car, sequential box. GTR 2004 class: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Audi V8 quattro DTM.name: Audi V8 quattro DTM
ams2:Audi V8 quattro DTM.notes: 1990-92 DTM Audi V8: 3.6 V8 at about 460 hp, 9500 rpm, quattro, straight-cut 6-speed dog box, the heavy sedan that beat the M3s. The Audi ran ABS; no TC in those years.

ams2:BMW M3 Sport Evo Group A.name: BMW M3 Sport Evo Group A
ams2:BMW M3 Sport Evo Group A.notes: The 2.5 Sport Evolution Group A car, the same engine and box as the AC E30 DTM entry. Values copied. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evo II DT.name: Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evo II DTM
ams2:Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evo II DT.notes: Same car as the AC 190E Evo II DTM. Values copied. ABS yes (AMG ran it from 1992), no TC.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette GTP.name: Chevrolet Corvette GTP
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette GTP.notes: 1980s IMSA GTP Corvette (the Lola-built car) in the NA 6.0 V8 form the wiki gives: 802 hp, 5-speed dogleg H-pattern (straight-cut dog box, whine 1.0), 1015 kg. A roaring small-block prototype. Nothing electronic (wiki).

ams2:Nissan R89C.name: Nissan R89C
ams2:Nissan R89C.notes: 1989 Group C: VRH35Z 3.5 twin-turbo V8, about 800 hp in race trim, 5-speed straight-cut dog box: two big turbos dumping on lift (1.8), heavy boost shunt. Group C: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Porsche 962C.name: Porsche 962C
ams2:Porsche 962C.notes: Same car as the AC 962C. Values copied. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Sauber Mercedes C9.name: Sauber Mercedes C9
ams2:Sauber Mercedes C9.notes: Same car as the AC Sauber C9. Values copied. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Audi R8 LMP1.name: Audi R8 LMP1
ams2:Audi R8 LMP1.notes: The 2000-05 Audi R8: 3.6 twin-turbo FSI V8 at about 610 hp restricted, Ricardo six-speed sequential paddles (the first pneumatic paddle shift at Le Mans). Turbo dump on lift. LMP1 of 2005 ran TC; no ABS.

ams2:Courage C60 Hybrid.name: Courage C60 Hybrid
ams2:Courage C60 Hybrid.notes: 2005 Courage C60 Hybrid with the Judd 4.0 V10 at 599 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 1004 kg: a screaming NA V10 prototype. Wiki: no TC, no ABS.

ams2:Dallara SP1.name: Dallara SP1
ams2:Dallara SP1.notes: Dallara SP1 with the Judd GV4 4.0 V10 at 599 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 1050 kg. Wiki: no TC, no ABS.

ams2:Lola B05/40 Turbo.name: Lola B05/40 Turbo
ams2:Lola B05/40 Turbo.notes: LMP2 2005 Lola with the AER 2.0 turbo four (about 500 hp): a big turbo four, shaky at idle and violent on lift (1.7). 6-speed sequential paddles. No TC, no ABS (as the V8 sister, wiki).

ams2:Lola B05/40 V8.name: Lola B05/40 V8
ams2:Lola B05/40 V8.notes: LMP2 2005 Lola with the Zytek 3.4 V8 at 548 hp (wiki), 6-speed sequential paddles, 896 kg. Wiki: no TC, no ABS.

ams2:Alpine A424.name: Alpine A424
ams2:Alpine A424.notes: LMDh: Mecachrome 3.4 single-turbo V6 at the 680 hp class cap with the spec Bosch hybrid on the rear axle, Xtrac seven-speed sequential. The hybrid fill tames the lift (1.3). LMDh: TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Aston Martin Valkyrie Hypercar.name: Aston Martin Valkyrie Hypercar
ams2:Aston Martin Valkyrie Hypercar.notes: The only non-hybrid Hypercar: Cosworth 6.5 NA V12 at the class cap, 11000 rpm, Xtrac seven-speed sequential. The V12 scream of an F1 car with no inertia. Hypercar: TC on, no ABS.

ams2:BMW M Hybrid V8.name: BMW M Hybrid V8
ams2:BMW M Hybrid V8.notes: LMDh: P66/3 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8 (from the DTM M4) at the 680 hp cap plus the spec hybrid, Xtrac seven-speed. Turbo V8 rumble, hybrid-tamed lift. TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Cadillac V-Series.R.name: Cadillac V-Series.R
ams2:Cadillac V-Series.R.notes: LMDh: ECR 5.5 NA cross-plane V8 at the cap plus the spec hybrid, Xtrac seven-speed: the loudest, lumpiest engine in the class, a big overrun bark. TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Lamborghini SC63.name: Lamborghini SC63
ams2:Lamborghini SC63.notes: LMDh: 3.8 twin-turbo cold-V V8 at the cap plus the spec hybrid, Xtrac seven-speed. TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Porsche 963.name: Porsche 963
ams2:Porsche 963.notes: LMDh: the 4.6 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 descended from the 918's RS Spyder engine, at the cap plus the spec hybrid, Xtrac seven-speed. Flat-plane buzz with turbos. TC on, no ABS.

ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 3.8.name: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 3.8
ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 3.8.notes: 997 GT3 Cup: 3.8 flat-six at about 450 hp, 8500 rpm, six-speed sequential dog box. Cup cars run without ABS or TC.

ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 4.0.name: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 4.0
ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup 4.0.notes: The 4.0 GT3 Cup: 4.0 NA flat-six at about 485 hp, 8500 rpm, race exhaust (pops 0.8), six-speed sequential dog box, straight cut (whine 0.9). Same values as the AC GT3 Cup 2017 and the AMS2 992 Cup. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (992).name: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (992)
ams2:Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (992).notes: 991/992 GT3 Cup 4.0: 4.0 flat-six at 485 to 510 hp, same six-speed sequential. Same values as the AC GT3 Cup 2017. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Caterham 620R.name: Caterham 620R
ams2:Caterham 620R.notes: 620R: supercharged 2.0 Duratec at 310 hp in 545 kg with the engine bolted to the tub under your knees: everything comes through, a supercharger bypass sigh on lift (1.2, turbo flag off), six-speed sequential (whine 0.8). No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Caterham Academy.name: Caterham Academy
ams2:Caterham Academy.notes: Academy race Seven: 1.6 Ford Sigma at 135 hp, five-speed H-pattern, live axle, 540 kg. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Caterham Superlight.name: Caterham Superlight
ams2:Caterham Superlight.notes: Superlight 360R: 2.0 Duratec at 180 hp, 7500 rpm, five-speed H-pattern with a close-ratio set, 560 kg. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Caterham Supersport.name: Caterham Supersport
ams2:Caterham Supersport.notes: Supersport race 360R: the same 2.0 Duratec and box as the Superlight in the Caterham race series trim. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Aussie Racing Camaro.name: Aussie Racing Camaro
ams2:Aussie Racing Camaro.notes: Aussie Racing Cars: a 5/8-scale Camaro silhouette on a Yamaha FJR1300 1.3 motorcycle inline-four (wiki, 89 kW), 6-speed sequential bike box, 595 kg: all buzz to 9000 rpm, no inertia, chain-drive shunt. No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:MINI Cooper JCW.name: MINI Cooper JCW
ams2:MINI Cooper JCW.notes: JCW class MINI Cooper (F56 JCW): 2.0 turbo four at 231 hp, six-speed manual, the JCW exhaust pops on the overrun. Road car: ABS and DSC on. Roster name is just MINI Cooper (class JCW); the 1965 Cooper S cars are separate entries.

ams2:BMW M1 Procar.name: BMW M1 Procar
ams2:BMW M1 Procar.notes: 1979 Procar: M88/1 3.5 24-valve inline-six at 470 hp, 9000 rpm, on Kugelfischer injection with a slide throttle (lumpy idle, lope 0.35), straight-cut ZF five-speed dog box (whine 1.0), mid-mounted. 1979: nothing electronic.

ams2:Maserati GranSport Trofeo.name: Maserati GranSport Trofeo
ams2:Maserati GranSport Trofeo.notes: 2005 one-make Trofeo: 4.2 cross-plane V8 at about 420 hp with the Cambiocorsa single-clutch automated manual (hard shifts, shunt 0.7, synchro shape). Trofeo kept ABS and TC.

ams2:Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct.name: Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct
ams2:Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct.notes: Direct-drive 125 cc single-cylinder two-stroke (wiki, 32 hp, 155 kg): one firing every revolution, so layout two-stroke with 1 cylinder; the whole kart buzzes at the firing rate, no inertia, a two-stroke's ragged overrun (pops 0.8, lope 0.4). Direct drive: no clutch, no gears, so the clutch and lug mixes are zero and only the chain-lash shunt plays. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter.name: Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter
ams2:Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter.notes: KZ-style 125 cc shifter kart: the same single-cylinder two-stroke at about 45 hp with a 6-speed sequential motorcycle gearbox and a manual clutch (launch judder is real on these), chain-lash shunt. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Kart 4-Stroke Race.name: Kart 4-Stroke Race
ams2:Kart 4-Stroke Race.notes: Four-stroke race kart (Honda GX-class single, about 15 to 20 hp): one firing every two revs, a thumping single with a centrifugal clutch (no clutch or lug effects) and chain lash. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Kart 4-Stroke Rental.name: Kart 4-Stroke Rental
ams2:Kart 4-Stroke Rental.notes: GX390 rental kart: 390 cc four-stroke single at 13 hp with a soft governor-style limiter, centrifugal clutch. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Super Kart 250cc.name: Super Kart 250cc
ams2:Super Kart 250cc.notes: 250 cc twin-cylinder two-stroke superkart, about 90 hp, 13000 rpm, 6-speed sequential: two firings per rev, the most frantic buzz in the game, screaming two-stroke overrun. No TC, no ABS.

ams2:Citroen DS3RX.name: Citroen DS3RX
ams2:Citroen DS3RX.notes: World RX Supercar: 2.0 turbo four at 600 hp with anti-lag, AWD, Sadev six-speed sequential dog box. Anti-lag bangs constantly on the overrun (pops 1.0), the lift is a cannon shot (1.8), heavy shunt through the AWD driveline. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Mini Countryman R60 RX.name: Mini Countryman R60 RX
ams2:Mini Countryman R60 RX.notes: World RX Countryman: the same 2.0 turbo anti-lag four, AWD and Sadev sequential. RX values. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Mitsubishi Lancer Evo10 RX.name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evo10 RX
ams2:Mitsubishi Lancer Evo10 RX.notes: World RX Evo X: 2.0 4B11 turbo anti-lag four, AWD, sequential. RX values. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Volkswagen Polo RX.name: Volkswagen Polo RX
ams2:Volkswagen Polo RX.notes: World RX Polo: 2.0 turbo anti-lag four, AWD, sequential. RX values. No ABS, no TC.

ams2:Super Trophy Trucks.name: Super Trophy Truck
ams2:Super Trophy Trucks.notes: Trophy truck: 6.8 litre NA V8 at 634 hp (wiki), 3-speed sequential stick, 1400 kg. A big-block lope and heavy pulses, a three-speed with huge driveline lash and long travel driveshafts (shunt 0.9). No TC, no ABS (wiki).

ams2:Lamborghini Veneno Roadster.name: Lamborghini Veneno Roadster
ams2:Lamborghini Veneno Roadster.notes: The Aventador-based Veneno: 6.5 V12 at 750 hp with the ISR single-clutch box that slams its shifts (shunt 0.7). Same values as the AC Aventador SV. Road car: ABS and ESC on.

ams2:Lamborghini Revuelto.name: Lamborghini Revuelto
ams2:Lamborghini Revuelto.notes: 6.5 V12 at 825 hp plus three motors for 1015 hp, 9500 rpm, eight-speed DCT: the V12 scream with electric fill softening the lift. Road car: ABS and ESC on.

ams2:Aston Martin Valkyrie.name: Aston Martin Valkyrie
ams2:Aston Martin Valkyrie.notes: Road Valkyrie: Cosworth 6.5 V12 at 1000 hp and 11100 rpm plus a small hybrid, seven-speed single-clutch sequential (dog-shaped shifts, straight-cut gears audible). An F1-grade V12 in a road car. ABS and TC on.

ams2:Brabham BT62.name: Brabham BT62
ams2:Brabham BT62.notes: Track-only BT62: 5.4 NA quad-cam V8 (Ford Coyote-derived) at 700 hp, 7400 rpm, Holinger six-speed sequential dog box (whine 0.9), race exhaust. Track car with ABS and TC.

ams2:McLaren Senna.name: McLaren Senna
ams2:McLaren Senna.notes: M840TR 4.0 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 at 800 hp, seven-speed DCT, Inconel exhaust that pops. Road car: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Audi R8 V10 GT.name: Audi R8 V10 GT
ams2:Audi R8 V10 GT.notes: 2023 R8 GT: 5.2 V10 at 620 hp, rear-drive, S tronic DCT. Same values as the AC R8 V10 Plus. Road car: ABS and ESC on.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C8 Z06.name: Chevrolet Corvette C8 Z06
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C8 Z06.notes: C8 Z06: LT6 5.5 flat-plane V8 at 670 hp and 8600 rpm, eight-speed DCT: the first screaming road Corvette. Road car: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Dodge Viper ACR.name: Dodge Viper ACR
ams2:Dodge Viper ACR.notes: 8.4 pushrod V10 at 645 hp and only 6200 rpm: the truck-derived ten's odd-fire lope (rock 0.8), heavy pulses at 15 Hz, six-speed Tremec manual with big lash. Road car: ABS and ESC on.

ams2:Maserati GT2 Stradale.name: Maserati GT2 Stradale
ams2:Maserati GT2 Stradale.notes: MC20-based GT2 Stradale: Nettuno 3.0 twin-turbo V6 at 640 hp, eight-speed DCT, turbo flutter on lift. Road car: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren F1 LM.name: McLaren F1 LM
ams2:McLaren F1 LM.notes: F1 LM: the unrestricted GTR engine, BMW S70/2 6.1 V12 at 680 hp, 7800 rpm, six-speed manual H-pattern with the GTR's straight-cut-ish gear set (whine 0.3), open exhaust. 1995 road car: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Ultima GTR.name: Ultima GTR
ams2:Ultima GTR.notes: Road Ultima GTR 640: 6.2 LS V8 at 640 hp in a 1000 kg kit car with a Porsche G50 transaxle (five-speed, some whine). Kit car: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Chevrolet Camaro SS.name: Chevrolet Camaro SS
ams2:Chevrolet Camaro SS.notes: Sixth-generation Camaro SS: LT1 6.2 V8 at 455 hp, six-speed manual. Same values as the AC C7 Stingray (same engine). Road car: ABS and TC on.

ams2:LamborghiniHuracanLP6202SuperTrofeo.name: LamborghiniHuracanLP6202SuperTrofeo
ams2:LamborghiniHuracanLP6202SuperTrofeo.notes: Super Trofeo EVO2: 5.2 V10 at 620 hp, X-trac sequential. Same values as the AC Super Trofeo. ABS and TC on.

ams2:Lamborghini Diablo SV-R Super Trofe.name: Lamborghini Diablo SV-R Super Trofeo
ams2:Lamborghini Diablo SV-R Super Trofe.notes: 1996 Diablo SV-R one-make racer: 5.7 V12 at 540 hp, five-speed manual H-pattern with the Countach-style forward gearbox (whine 0.5, lash), open exhaust. Stripped 1990s race car: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:BMW 2002 Turbo.name: BMW 2002 Turbo
ams2:BMW 2002 Turbo.notes: 1973 2002 Turbo: Europe's first turbo production car, 2.0 four with a KKK turbo and no wastegate finesse, 170 hp with a cliff-edge lag (lift-off 1.6, shunt 0.7), four-speed H-pattern. 1973: nothing electronic.

ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.name: Chevrolet Corvette C3
ams2:Chevrolet Corvette C3.notes: Road C3 big-block: 427 V8 at about 390 hp on a Holley, 4-speed Muncie: the full muscle-car lope (rock 0.95), heavy pulses at 14 Hz, big flywheel, lots of lash. 1969: nothing electronic.

ams2:Lamborghini Miura SV.name: Lamborghini Miura SV
ams2:Lamborghini Miura SV.notes: Same car as the AC Miura SV. Values copied. Nothing electronic.

ams2:Lotus 23.name: Lotus 23
ams2:Lotus 23.notes: 1962 Lotus 23: Lotus-Ford 1.5 twin-cam four on Webers, about 140 hp, in a 450 kg spaceframe with a Hewland five-speed straight-cut box (whine 0.8). Carburettor idle lope. 1962: nothing electronic.

ams2:MINI Cooper S.name: MINI Cooper S
ams2:MINI Cooper S.notes: Vintage Touring Tier 2 Cooper S: the 1275 A-series on twin SUs, gearbox-in-sump whine (0.5), four-speed H-pattern, front-driven. Same values as the Copa Classic B 1965 car. Nothing electronic.

ams2:BMW V12 LMR.name: BMW V12 LMR
ams2:BMW V12 LMR.notes: 1999 Le Mans winner: the McLaren F1 GTR's BMW S70 6.0 V12 at about 580 hp restricted, 7000 rpm, six-speed sequential X-trac (straight cut, whine 0.9), open prototype. A V12 scream with a race exhaust. 1999 LMP: TC yes, no ABS.

ams2:Ferrari 250 GTO.name: Ferrari 250 GTO
ams2:Ferrari 250 GTO.notes: 1962 250 GTO: Colombo 3.0 V12 on six Webers, about 300 hp, 7500 rpm, five-speed manual with straight-cut lower gears (whine 0.5), a carburettor lope at idle. 1962: nothing electronic.

ams2:Ferrari 488 GT3.name: Ferrari 488 GT3
ams2:Ferrari 488 GT3.notes: 488 GT3: 3.9 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 BoP'd to about 550 hp, Hewland six-speed sequential (straight cut, whine 0.8), turbo flutter on lift. GT3: ABS and TC on.

ams2:Lotus Exige V6 Cup.name: Lotus Exige V6 Cup
ams2:Lotus Exige V6 Cup.notes: Exige V6 Cup: Toyota 2GR 3.5 V6 with an Edelbrock supercharger at 350 hp, six-speed manual H-pattern, a mid-mounted engine right behind the seat. Supercharger bypass sigh on lift (1.2, turbo flag off). Cup car with ABS and switchable TC: both on.

ams2:Nissan Skyline Super Silhouette.name: Nissan Skyline Super Silhouette
ams2:Nissan Skyline Super Silhouette.notes: 1983 Group 5 Skyline R30: LZ20B 2.1 turbo four at about 570 hp with a huge turbo and no restraint, 7600 rpm, five-speed straight-cut dog box (whine 0.9). The most violent lift in the set (2.0) and flames on every overrun (pops 1.0). Nothing electronic.

ams2:Toyota GT-One (1999).name: Toyota GT-One (1999)
ams2:Toyota GT-One (1999).notes: TS020 GT-One: R36V 3.6 twin-turbo V8 at about 600 hp restricted, 7000 rpm, six-speed sequential (straight cut), the 1999 GT1-prototype. Turbo flutter on lift. TC yes, no ABS.

ams2:VRC Auriel 90 GTO.name: VRC Auriel 90 GTO
ams2:VRC Auriel 90 GTO.notes: Reiza's IMSA GTO-era silhouette in the Mazda RX-7 GTO mould: a four-rotor rotary (4 x 654 cc) at about 600 hp, 9000 rpm, five-speed straight-cut dog box (whine 0.9). Rotary: no reciprocating mass, all scream (buzz 1.0, thump carrier high and light), bangs on the overrun (pops 0.9). 1990 IMSA: no ABS, no TC.

ams2:Renault Clio Cup.name: Renault Clio Cup
ams2:Renault Clio Cup.notes: Clio IV Cup: 1.6 turbo four at 220 hp, six-speed Sadev sequential (whine 0.7), a one-make front-driver. Turbo flutter on lift. Cup car with ABS, no TC.

ams2:FIA-GT1 Nissan GT-R GT1.name: FIA-GT1 Nissan GT-R GT1
ams2:FIA-GT1 Nissan GT-R GT1.notes: 2010 FIA GT1 World Championship GT-R: the VK56 5.6 NA V8 at about 600 hp (the road car's twin-turbo V6 was not allowed), 7000 rpm, Ricardo six-speed sequential (straight cut, whine 0.9). GT1 2010: ABS and TC on.

ams2:McLaren F1 Track Days.name: McLaren F1 Track Days
ams2:McLaren F1 Track Days.notes: The road McLaren F1 in its track-day listing: BMW S70/2 6.1 V12 at 627 hp, 7500 rpm, six-speed manual H-pattern, no driver aids at all (1993 road car: no ABS, no TC).

lmu:Alpine_A424_2024.name: Alpine A424
lmu:Alpine_A424_2024.notes: LMDh: Alpine-modified Mecachrome V634, a 3.4 litre 90-degree single-turbo V6 (the only single turbo in the class) at 500 kW by BoP, seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (Wikipedia Alpine A424, LMU car page). The hybrid is the LMDh spec Bosch 50 kW unit at the rear axle; the Engine tile plays only the V6. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Alpine A424 (same real car). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited by the rules.

lmu:Aston_Martin_Valkyrie_2025.name: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR-LMH
lmu:Aston_Martin_Valkyrie_2025.notes: LMH: Cosworth 6.5 litre NA V12 at 500 kW, seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (LMU car page). The race car runs without the road Valkyrie's hybrid, so the Engine tile plays the whole powertrain. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Aston Martin Valkyrie Hypercar (same real car): an F1-style V12 scream with little inertia. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:BMW_M_Hybrid_V8_2023.name: BMW M Hybrid V8
lmu:BMW_M_Hybrid_V8_2023.notes: LMDh: P66/3 4.0 litre twin-turbo V8 (from the DTM M4), about 650 bhp, seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). The spec Bosch 50 kW rear hybrid is not played by the Engine tile. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 BMW M Hybrid V8 (same real car). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Cadillac_V-lmdh_2023.name: Cadillac V-Series.R
lmu:Cadillac_V-lmdh_2023.notes: LMDh: LMC55R 5.5 litre (5463 cc) NA 90-degree V8 with a cross-plane crank, revving to about 8800 (Wikipedia LMC55R, Hagerty, Motor1), Xtrac seven-speed. The spec Bosch 50 kW rear hybrid is not played. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Cadillac V-Series.R (same real car); the cross-plane crank is confirmed, so the lumpy rumble and big overrun bark stand. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Ferrari_499P_2023.name: Ferrari 499P
lmu:Ferrari_499P_2023.notes: LMH: F163CG 2992 cc 120-degree twin-turbo V6, a stressed member, Xtrac seven-speed sequential (Wikipedia Ferrari 499P, Ferrari). Hybrid: a 200 kW front-axle ERS, not played by the Engine tile; the entry keeps the rear-driven default since the front axle only drives above a speed threshold. Starting point: derived from the AMS2 Alpine A424 (turbo V6 Hypercar) with the even-firing 120-degree vee smoothed (rock 0.4, lope 0.15) and the thump carrier of the AC/AMS2 Ferrari 488 GT3 (26 Hz); lift 1.2 sits between the LMDh cars (1.3) and the big-hybrid AC LMP1s (0.9). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Genesis_GMR001_2026.name: Genesis GMR-001
lmu:Genesis_GMR001_2026.notes: LMDh (WEC from 2026): Genesis G8MR 3.2 litre twin-turbo V8 by Hyundai Motorsport, about 60 % of its parts shared with the WRC 1.6 four, about 680 hp with the hybrid, Xtrac seven-speed, 1030 kg (Wikipedia, LMU car page, The Drive). The spec Bosch 50 kW hybrid is not played (LMU's page says front-mounted; LMDh rules and 24h-lemans.com put it at the rear). Crank type unpublished. Starting point: the AMS2 Lamborghini SC63 (twin-turbo V8 LMDh) for a smaller, faster engine (inertia 0.4, limiter 14 Hz, thump carrier 22 Hz). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Isotta_Tipo6_2024.name: Isotta Fraschini Tipo 6 LMH-C
lmu:Isotta_Tipo6_2024.notes: LMH, raced the 2024 WEC only: 2999 cc 90-degree twin-turbo V6 tuned with HWA, Bosch front-axle hybrid, 900 V battery, Xtrac seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (Wikipedia Isotta Fraschini Tipo 6 LMH-C, LMU car page). The hybrid is not played; rear-driven default kept. Starting point: derived from the AMS2 Alpine A424 (turbo V6 Hypercar), lift 1.2 for the front-axle harvest as on the other LMH hybrids here. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Lamborghini_SC63_2024.name: Lamborghini SC63
lmu:Lamborghini_SC63_2024.notes: LMDh: 3.8 litre twin-turbo V8 at 520 kW listed, seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (LMU car page). The spec Bosch 50 kW rear hybrid is not played. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Lamborghini SC63 (same real car). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Peugeot_9x8_2023.name: Peugeot 9X8
lmu:Peugeot_9x8_2023.notes: LMH, the original wingless 2022-2023 car: X6H 2.6 litre 90-degree twin-turbo V6 capped at 8500 rpm, about 500 kW to the rear, a 200 kW front-axle motor, Sadev seven-speed sequential (Wikipedia Peugeot 9X8). The hybrid is not played; rear-driven default kept. Starting point: derived from the AMS2 Alpine A424 (turbo V6 Hypercar); the smallest engine in the class, so a lighter thump (0.55), less inertia (0.35) and a higher carrier (26 Hz). Same values as Peugeot_9x8_2024: the 2024 car changed body and tyres, not the powertrain. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Peugeot_9x8_2024.name: Peugeot 9X8 2024
lmu:Peugeot_9x8_2024.notes: LMH, the 2024 evolution: a rear wing and about 90 % new bodywork (LMU car page), narrower fronts and wider rears (29 / 34 cm) in place of equal 31 cm tyres (Wikipedia). Same X6H 2.6 litre twin-turbo V6, 200 kW front-axle motor (not played) and Sadev seven-speed as the 2023 car. Starting point: identical to Peugeot_9x8_2023 (derived there from the AMS2 Alpine A424), since nothing the engine or driveline tiles model changed. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Porsche_963_2023.name: Porsche 963
lmu:Porsche_963_2023.notes: LMDh: 4.6 litre twin-turbo flat-plane V8 from the RS Spyder / 918 family, 500 kW, seven-speed sequential, 1030 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). The spec Bosch 50 kW rear hybrid is not played. Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Porsche 963 (same real car). Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:SGC_007_2023.name: Glickenhaus SCG 007 LMH
lmu:SGC_007_2023.notes: LMH (the folder is spelt SGC): Pipo Moteurs 3.5 litre 90-degree twin-turbo V8, 9000 rpm redline, about 670 bhp, no hybrid, Xtrac paddle-shift sequential (seven-speed per Wikipedia and the LMU page, six per one spec sheet) (Wikipedia Glickenhaus SCG 007 LMH, LMU car page). Starting point: the AMS2 Lamborghini SC63 (twin-turbo V8 Hypercar) with no hybrid to fill the lift, so a bigger turbo dump (1.5, towards the GT3 turbo V8s at 1.6). Not the AC SCG 003C, a different car and engine. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Toyota_GR10_2023.name: Toyota GR010 Hybrid
lmu:Toyota_GR10_2023.notes: LMH: Toyota H8909 3.5 litre 90-degree twin-turbo V6 at 500 kW, an Aisin-Denso 200 kW front-axle motor, Toyota/Aisin transverse seven-speed sequential (Wikipedia Toyota GR010 Hybrid). The hybrid is not played; rear-driven default kept. Starting point: derived from the AMS2 Alpine A424 (turbo V6 Hypercar), lift 1.2 as on the other LMH hybrids here; not the AC TS040, whose NA V8 is a different engine. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:Vandervell_680_2023.name: Vanwall Vandervell 680
lmu:Vandervell_680_2023.notes: LMH, raced the 2023 WEC only: Gibson GL458 4.5 litre NA 90-degree V8, no hybrid, Xtrac P1159C six-speed sequential, 1030 kg (Wikipedia Vanwall Vandervell 680, LMU car page). Starting point: the AMS2 Oreca 07 (the LMP2 Gibson GK428, same maker, NA race V8) grown to 4.5 litres (thump 0.7), with the Hypercar driveline used for the other cars here. Hypercar: TC on, ABS prohibited.

lmu:ADESS_AD25_2026.name: ADESS AD25
lmu:ADESS_AD25_2026.notes: LMP3 Gen 3, free in LMU v1.3.3 (the LMU cars index titles its page ADESS-03); raced in the Le Mans Cup by Nielsen Racing rather than the ELMS. The class's spec Toyota 3.5 twin-turbo V6 and six-speed sequential, mechanically identical to the other three LMP3s, only the bodywork differs (Racecontrol). Starting point: identical to Ligier_JSP325_2025, derived there from the AMS2 Ligier JS P320. LMP3: TC on, no ABS.

lmu:Duqueine_D09LMP3_2026.name: Duqueine D09
lmu:Duqueine_D09LMP3_2026.notes: LMP3 Gen 3 (LMU ELMS Pack 3): Toyota V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 (3445 cc, sold as 3.5) at about 470 bhp, six-speed sequential, about 1000 kg minimum (LMU car page); the spec powertrain, only the chassis differs. Starting point: identical to Ligier_JSP325_2025, derived there from the AMS2 Ligier JS P320. LMP3: TC on, no ABS.

lmu:Ginetta_G61Evo_2025.name: Ginetta G61-LT-P3 Evo
lmu:Ginetta_G61Evo_2025.notes: LMP3 Gen 3 (LMU's page spells it G61-LT-P325-Evo): the spec Toyota V35A twin-turbo V6 (3445 cc, sold as 3.5) at about 470 bhp and six-speed sequential (LMU car page, Racecontrol); only the chassis differs from the other three LMP3s here (left-hand drive, rotates more freely). Starting point: identical to Ligier_JSP325_2025, derived there from the AMS2 Ligier JS P320. LMP3: TC on, no ABS.

lmu:Ligier_JSP325_2025.name: Ligier JS P325
lmu:Ligier_JSP325_2025.notes: LMP3 Gen 3: Toyota V35A-FTS, a production-based 3445 cc 60-degree twin-turbo V6 (sold as 3.5) at about 470 hp, Xtrac P1152 six-speed sequential with pneumatic paddles, Magneti Marelli electronics (Wikipedia Ligier JS P325, Ligier); engine and box are spec across the class. Starting point: the driveline of the AMS2 Ligier JS P320 (its Gen 2 predecessor, same class and sequential) with the engine re-derived for a production twin-turbo V6 (buzz 0.8, lift 1.5 as the AMS2 turbo V6 prototypes, lug 0.4). LMP3: TC on, no ABS (Racecontrol and Coach Dave Academy LMU LMP3 guides).

lmu:Oreca_07_ELMS_2023.name: Oreca 07 Gibson (ELMS)
lmu:Oreca_07_ELMS_2023.notes: LMP2 in ELMS trim (LMU's ELMS packs): the unrestricted Gibson GK428 4.2 litre NA V8 at about 600 hp, high-downforce aero at every track, 20 kg lighter than the WEC car, same six-speed sequential (Coach Dave Academy, Racecontrol). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Oreca 07 (same real car), identical to Oreca_07_LM_2023 for the reason given there. LMP2: TC on, no ABS (Coach Dave Academy's ELMS Oreca guide).

lmu:Oreca_07_LM_2023.name: Oreca 07 Gibson (WEC)
lmu:Oreca_07_LM_2023.notes: LMP2 in WEC / Le Mans trim (LMU's 2023 and 2024 WEC Oreca): Gibson GK428 4.2 litre NA V8, six-speed sequential, 930 kg listed (LMU car page); in WEC trim it is restricted to about 560 hp, runs the low-downforce Le Mans kit everywhere and is 20 kg heavier than the ELMS car (Coach Dave Academy, Racecontrol). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Oreca 07 (same real car). Identical to Oreca_07_ELMS_2023: power, weight and aero are the only differences and none of them is something the engine or driveline tiles model. LMP2: TC on, no ABS.

lmu:911GT3R_2024.name: Porsche 911 GT3 R (992)
lmu:911GT3R_2024.notes: LMGT3: 4.2 litre NA flat-six at about 565 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1317 kg (LMU car page). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Porsche 992 GT3-R (same real car), itself from the AC 911 GT3 R 2016. GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Aston_Martin_Vantage_AMR_2023.name: Aston Martin Vantage AMR GTE
lmu:Aston_Martin_Vantage_AMR_2023.notes: GTE (LMU calls it Aston Martin Vantage AMR, in the GTE class): 4.0 litre twin-turbo V8 (AMG-sourced), 500 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1245 kg (LMU car page). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Aston Martin Vantage GTE (same real car). GTE: ABS and TC on.

lmu:BMW_M4_LMGT3_2023.name: BMW M4 LMGT3
lmu:BMW_M4_LMGT3_2023.notes: LMGT3: P58 3.0 litre twin-turbo inline-six, Xtrac six-speed sequential (AMS2 pass from the AMS2 wiki infobox). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 BMW M4 GT3 (same real car): a smooth six with two turbos that breathe hard on lift. GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Chevrolet_C8R_LM_2023.name: Chevrolet Corvette C8.R
lmu:Chevrolet_C8R_LM_2023.notes: GTE: 5.5 litre NA flat-plane V8, 500 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1240 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Chevrolet Corvette C8.R (same real car); not the AC C7.R, whose cross-plane V8 rumbles. GTE: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Corvette_Z06GT3R_2023.name: Corvette Z06 LMGT3.R
lmu:Corvette_Z06GT3R_2023.notes: LMGT3 (a 2024 car in a 2023-named folder): 5.5 litre NA V8, the LT6-based flat-plane, six-speed sequential, 1344 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R (same real car): a flat-plane scream, not the C7.R's cross-plane rumble. GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Ferrari_296GT3_2023.name: Ferrari 296 LMGT3
lmu:Ferrari_296GT3_2023.notes: LMGT3: F163 2992 cc 120-degree twin-turbo V6 with the turbos in the vee, no hybrid (GT3 rules), about 600 hp before BoP, a new Xtrac six-speed transverse sequential with electric shift (Ferrari launch material via evo and Race Engine Technology; LMU's page rounds to 2.9 litres). Starting point: the AC 488 GT3 Evo 2020 / AMS2 Ferrari 488 GT3 values (same maker, twin-turbo Ferrari GT3) with a V6's lighter thump (0.6) and the smoother even-firing 120-degree vee (rock 0.4). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Ferrari_488GTE_LM_2023.name: Ferrari 488 GTE Evo
lmu:Ferrari_488GTE_LM_2023.notes: GTE: F154 3.9 litre (3902 cc; LMU's page rounds to 4.0) twin-turbo flat-plane V8, 500 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1245 kg (LMU car page). Starting point: the same values as the AC Ferrari 488 GT3 (same engine family: flat-plane buzz, turbo flutter and dump on lift). GTE: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Ford_Mustang_GT3_2024.name: Ford Mustang LMGT3
lmu:Ford_Mustang_GT3_2024.notes: LMGT3: 5.4 litre NA Coyote-based cross-plane V8 built by M-Sport (production block and heads, dry sump), about 550 bhp, Xtrac six-speed rear transaxle, 1329 kg (Ford Performance, Multimatic, LMU car page). Starting point: the AC/AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT3 (NA cross-plane V8 GT3) scaled to 5.4 litres (rock 0.75, thump 0.95, buzz 0.7). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Lamborghini_Huracan_GT3_2024.name: Lamborghini Huracan LMGT3 Evo2
lmu:Lamborghini_Huracan_GT3_2024.notes: LMGT3: 5.2 litre NA V10 and X-trac six-speed sequential (AMS2 pass; LMU cars index). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2 and the AC Huracan GT3 (same engine and box). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:LexusRCF_GT3_2024.name: Lexus RC F LMGT3
lmu:LexusRCF_GT3_2024.notes: LMGT3: 5.4 litre NA V8, an enlarged 2UR-GSE (the road RC F's 4968 cc V8), about 500 bhp, six-speed sequential (maker not found), 1355 kg (LMU car page, DriveArabia launch report, Toyota). Starting point: the Ford_Mustang_GT3_2024 values in this pack (same size NA cross-plane V8, themselves from the AC/AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT3), a touch smoother and higher revving (rock 0.7, thump 0.9, buzz 0.75). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:McLaren_720sGChallenge_2026.name: McLaren 720S LMGT3 Evo (Logitech G McLaren Challenge)
lmu:McLaren_720sGChallenge_2026.notes: Most likely the 720S LMGT3 Evo as run in the 2026 Logitech G McLaren Challenge, which moved to LMU for 2026 with that car (McLaren, Traxion). The folder name is the only link: the in-game display name and any spec change (BoP, fixed setup) are unconfirmed. Same M840T 4.0 litre twin-turbo V8 and Ricardo sequential, so starting point: the same values as McLaren_720sGT3Evo_2023 (from the AMS2 McLaren 720S GT3 EVO). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:McLaren_720sGT3Evo_2023.name: McLaren 720S LMGT3 Evo
lmu:McLaren_720sGT3Evo_2023.notes: LMGT3: M840T 4.0 litre twin-turbo flat-plane V8, about 600 bhp listed, Ricardo six-speed sequential, 1345 kg (LMU store listing, AMS2 pass). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 McLaren 720S GT3 EVO (same real car). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Mercedes_AMGGT3Evo_2025.name: Mercedes-AMG LMGT3
lmu:Mercedes_AMGGT3Evo_2025.notes: LMGT3, the GT3 Evo: M159 6.2 litre (6208 cc, badged 6.3 by AMG and LMU) NA cross-plane V8 with side exhausts, about 560 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1360 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO and the AC Mercedes AMG GT3 (same engine and box). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Porsche_911RSR-19_2023.name: Porsche 911 RSR-19
lmu:Porsche_911RSR-19_2023.notes: GTE: mid-mounted 4194 cc NA flat-six (the 2019 RSR's 4.2; LMU's page says 4.0, which is the 2017 RSR), about 510 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1243 kg (Porsche launch via evo India and The Drive, LMU car page). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Porsche 911 RSR-19 (same real car). GTE: ABS and TC on.

lmu:Vantage_AMR_GT3Evo_2024.name: Aston Martin Vantage AMR LMGT3
lmu:Vantage_AMR_GT3Evo_2024.notes: LMGT3 (the Vantage GT3 Evo): AMG-sourced 4.0 litre twin-turbo cross-plane V8, about 535 bhp, six-speed sequential, 1306 kg (LMU car page, AMS2 pass). Starting point: the same values as the AMS2 Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO (same real car). GT3: ABS and TC on.

lmu:992S_PC_2023.name: Porsche 911 Turbo S (992) Safety Car
lmu:992S_PC_2023.notes: Not a race car, and identified from the folder name only (unconfirmed in game): 992S_PC reads as the 992 Turbo S pace car, the Porsche 911 Turbo S (992) the WEC has used as its safety car since 2022 (Porsche newsroom, Sportscar365); no 992 Cup car appears in any LMU car list. 992 Turbo S: 3745 cc twin-turbo flat-six, 650 PS, eight-speed PDK (synchro-shaped shifts), all-wheel drive (the entry keeps the rear-driven default). Starting point: the same values as the AC Porsche 911 Turbo S (991, the same twin-turbo flat-six family and PDK), litres set to 3.7. Road car: ABS and PSM on.

acc:amr_v12_vantage_gt3.name: Aston Martin V12 Vantage GT3
acc:amr_v12_vantage_gt3.notes: 2012 Vantage GT3: modified production 6.0 NA V12, dry sump, about 600 bhp, Xtrac six-speed sequential with paddles (Aston Martin Racing 2011 specification). Starting point: engine values from the AMS2 Aston Martin DBR9 (the same 6.0 V12 family), driveline from the GT3 class (AC R8 LMS, Huracan GT3) rather than the GT1 car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:amr_v8_vantage_gt3.name: AMR V8 Vantage (2019)
acc:amr_v8_vantage_gt3.notes: 2019 Vantage GT3: AMG-sourced 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8, Xtrac six-speed sequential (Wikipedia, Aston Martin Vantage (2018)). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO (same engine and box). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:audi_r8_lms.name: Audi R8 LMS
acc:audi_r8_lms.notes: Second-generation R8 LMS (2015): 5.2 NA V10, six-speed sequential pneumatic box (Audi Sport technical data 2016). Starting point: same values as the AC R8 LMS 2016 (ac:ks_audi_r8_lms_2016) and the AMS2 Audi R8 LMS GT3, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:audi_r8_lms_evo.name: Audi R8 LMS Evo (2019)
acc:audi_r8_lms_evo.notes: 2019 R8 LMS GT3 evo: the same 5.2 NA V10 and six-speed sequential as the 2015 car. Starting point: same values as the AC R8 LMS 2016 (ac:ks_audi_r8_lms_2016). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:audi_r8_lms_evo_ii.name: Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II
acc:audi_r8_lms_evo_ii.notes: 2022 evo II: the same 5.2 NA V10 and six-speed sequential as the first R8 LMS. Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:bentley_continental_gt3_2016.name: Bentley Continental GT3 2016
acc:bentley_continental_gt3_2016.notes: First-generation Continental GT3 (the 2015 car): 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8, front-engined, Xtrac six-speed sequential (Dyson Racing spec page). Starting point: same values as the 2018 Bentley here, from the twin-turbo cross-plane V8 GT3 class (AMS2 BMW M6 GT3, AMS2 Vantage GT3 EVO). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:bentley_continental_gt3_2018.name: Bentley Continental GT3 2018
acc:bentley_continental_gt3_2018.notes: Second-generation Continental GT3: 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8, over 550 bhp unrestricted, front-engined, Ricardo six-speed sequential transaxle (Bentley media release 2018). Starting point: no same-car entry; class values of the other twin-turbo cross-plane V8 GT3s (AMS2 BMW M6 GT3, AMS2 Aston Martin Vantage GT3 EVO). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:bmw_m4_gt3.name: BMW M4 GT3
acc:bmw_m4_gt3.notes: P58 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six, six-speed sequential (BMW M Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 BMW M4 GT3, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:bmw_m6_gt3.name: BMW M6 GT3
acc:bmw_m6_gt3.notes: S63 4.4 twin-turbo cross-plane V8, six-speed sequential (BMW M Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 BMW M6 GT3, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:ferrari_296_gt3.name: Ferrari 296 GT3
acc:ferrari_296_gt3.notes: F163 3.0 (2992 cc) twin-turbo 120-degree V6, no hybrid in GT3 trim, about 600 hp before BoP, transverse Xtrac six-speed sequential (Ferrari launch 2022, Autoblog, Crank and Piston). Starting point: the twin-turbo V6 GT3 values of the AC GT-R GT3, with less rock and more buzz for the even-firing, high-revving 120-degree V6 (from the AC 488 GT3 flat-plane buzz). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:ferrari_488_gt3.name: Ferrari 488 GT3
acc:ferrari_488_gt3.notes: 2018 488 GT3: F154 3.9 twin-turbo flat-plane V8, six-speed sequential (Ferrari Competizioni GT). Starting point: same values as the AC 488 GT3 (ac:ks_ferrari_488_gt3), the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:ferrari_488_gt3_evo.name: Ferrari 488 GT3 Evo 2020
acc:ferrari_488_gt3_evo.notes: 488 GT3 Evo 2020: the same F154 3.9 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 and six-speed sequential as the 488 GT3. Starting point: same values as the AC 488 GT3 Evo 2020 (ac:ks_ferrari_488_gt3_2020), the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:ford_mustang_gt3.name: Ford Mustang GT3
acc:ford_mustang_gt3.notes: 2024 Mustang GT3 (ACC v1.10.2 bonus car): 5.4 NA Coyote-derived cross-plane V8 (M-Sport), dry sump, front-mid, rear Xtrac six-speed sequential transaxle (Multimatic Mustang GT3 overview 2024, Wikipedia). Starting point: the big NA cross-plane V8 GT3 values of the AC AMG GT3 (6.2), a touch less rock and lope for the smaller quad-cam engine. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:honda_nsx_gt3.name: Honda NSX GT3
acc:honda_nsx_gt3.notes: 2017 NSX GT3: 3.5 (3501 cc) twin-turbo 75-degree V6, longitudinal mid-engine, no hybrid, six-speed sequential to the rear wheels (Honda customer racing data, Acura launch 2016). Starting point: the twin-turbo V6 GT3 values of the AC GT-R GT3 (ac:ks_nissan_gtr_gt3). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:honda_nsx_gt3_evo.name: Honda NSX Evo (2019)
acc:honda_nsx_gt3_evo.notes: 2019 NSX GT3 Evo: the same 3.5 twin-turbo V6 and six-speed sequential as the 2017 car. Starting point: same values as the Honda NSX GT3 here (from the AC GT-R GT3). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:jaguar_g3.name: Jaguar G3
acc:jaguar_g3.notes: Emil Frey Racing's XK-based G3 (2012): Ilmor-prepared Jaguar AJ133 5.0 V8, front-engined, Xtrac six-speed sequential (Wikipedia, Emil Frey Racing). No source states the race engine's aspiration; taken as NA (no supercharger is mentioned in any race spec): confirm. Starting point: a big NA cross-plane V8 GT3, scaled down a little from the AC AMG GT3 (6.2). ABS and TC assumed on as across GT3, not separately confirmed for this car.

acc:lamborghini_gallardo_rex.name: Lamborghini Gallardo R-EX
acc:lamborghini_gallardo_rex.notes: Reiter Engineering R-EX (2017), built on the Gallardo LP560-4 GT3 FL2: 5.2 NA V10 (Top Gear NL, Italpassion), converted to rear-drive; earlier Reiter GT3 Gallardos ran a six-speed sequential, the R-EX gearbox supplier not confirmed. Starting point: same values as the AC Huracan GT3 and R8 LMS (the same 5.2 V10 family). ABS and TC assumed on as across GT3, not separately confirmed for this car.

acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3.name: Lamborghini Huracan GT3
acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3.notes: 2015 Huracan GT3: 5.2 NA V10, rear-drive, Xtrac six-speed sequential (Lamborghini Squadra Corse). Starting point: same values as the AC Huracan GT3 (ac:ks_lamborghini_huracan_gt3), the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3_evo.name: Lamborghini Huracan Evo (2019)
acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3_evo.notes: 2019 Huracan GT3 Evo: the same 5.2 NA V10 and Xtrac sequential as the 2015 car. Starting point: same values as the AC Huracan GT3 (ac:ks_lamborghini_huracan_gt3) and the AMS2 Huracan GT3 EVO2. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3_evo2.name: Lamborghini Huracan Evo2
acc:lamborghini_huracan_gt3_evo2.notes: 2023 Huracan GT3 EVO2: 5.2 NA V10, Xtrac six-speed sequential. Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Lamborghini Huracan GT3 EVO2, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:lexus_rc_f_gt3.name: Lexus RC F GT3
acc:lexus_rc_f_gt3.notes: RC F GT3: 5.4 NA V8 grown from the road 2UR-GSE 5.0, about 500 hp, six-speed sequential, rear-drive (ConceptCarz, Drive Arabia 2017). Starting point: a big NA cross-plane V8 GT3 from the AC AMG GT3, a little less lope for the quad-cam engine. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:mclaren_650s_gt3.name: McLaren 650S GT3
acc:mclaren_650s_gt3.notes: M838T 3.8 twin-turbo flat-plane V8, six-speed sequential (McLaren GT). Starting point: same values as the AC 650S GT3 (ac:ks_mclaren_650_gt3), the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:mclaren_720s_gt3.name: McLaren 720S GT3 (2019)
acc:mclaren_720s_gt3.notes: M840T 4.0 twin-turbo flat-plane V8, six-speed sequential (McLaren). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 McLaren 720S GT3, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:mclaren_720s_gt3_evo.name: McLaren 720S GT3 Evo 2023
acc:mclaren_720s_gt3_evo.notes: The 2023 EVO: the same M840T 4.0 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 and six-speed sequential as the 720S GT3. Starting point: same values as the AMS2 McLaren 720S GT3 EVO, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:mercedes_amg_gt3.name: Mercedes-AMG GT3
acc:mercedes_amg_gt3.notes: 2015 AMG GT3: M159 6.2 NA cross-plane V8, six-speed sequential transaxle (Mercedes-AMG customer racing). Starting point: same values as the AC AMG GT3 (ac:ks_mercedes_amg_gt3) and the AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT3, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:mercedes_amg_gt3_evo.name: Mercedes-AMG GT3 2020
acc:mercedes_amg_gt3_evo.notes: 2020 AMG GT3 Evo: the same M159 6.2 NA V8 and six-speed sequential as the 2015 car. Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO and the AC AMG GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:nissan_gt_r_gt3_2017.name: Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3 2017
acc:nissan_gt_r_gt3_2017.notes: The earlier GT-R Nismo GT3 (the 2015 car): the same VR38DETT 3.8 twin-turbo V6 and six-speed sequential as the 2018 car. Starting point: same values as the AC GT-R GT3 (ac:ks_nissan_gtr_gt3). GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:nissan_gt_r_gt3_2018.name: Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3 2018
acc:nissan_gt_r_gt3_2018.notes: 2018 GT-R Nismo GT3: VR38DETT 3.8 twin-turbo V6, rear-drive, six-speed sequential (Nismo). Starting point: same values as the AC GT-R GT3 (ac:ks_nissan_gtr_gt3) and the AMS2 Nissan GT-R Nismo GT3. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_991_gt3_r.name: Porsche 991 GT3 R
acc:porsche_991_gt3_r.notes: The 991.1 GT3 R (ACC lists it as the 2018 car): 4.0 NA flat-six at about 500 hp, six-speed sequential dog box (Porsche Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AC 911 GT3 R 2016 (ac:ks_porsche_911_gt3_r_2016), the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_991ii_gt3_r.name: Porsche 911II GT3 R (2019)
acc:porsche_991ii_gt3_r.notes: 991.2 GT3 R (2019): 4.0 NA flat-six at about 550 hp, six-speed sequential dog box (Porsche Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Porsche 911 GT3 R (the 991.2) and the AC GT3 R 2016. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_992_gt3_r.name: Porsche 992 GT3 R
acc:porsche_992_gt3_r.notes: 992 GT3 R (2023): 4.2 NA flat-six, six-speed sequential dog box (Porsche Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Porsche 992 GT3-R, the same car. GT3: ABS and TC on.

acc:alpine_a110_gt4.name: Alpine A110 GT4
acc:alpine_a110_gt4.notes: 2018 A110 GT4 (Signatech): the road car's 1.8 turbo inline-four reworked, 350 to 400 hp by BoP, mid-engined, six-speed sequential with paddles (Alpine, Top Gear 2018). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Alpine A110 GT4 EVO (same engine and box). GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:amr_v8_vantage_gt4.name: AMR V8 Vantage GT4
acc:amr_v8_vantage_gt4.notes: 2018 Vantage GT4: Mercedes-AMG M177 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8 (Wikipedia), Xtrac six-speed sequential, Alcon clutch, Bosch Motorsport ABS (Aston Martin Racing launch). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Aston Martin Vantage GT4 EVO (same engine and box). GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:audi_r8_gt4.name: Audi R8 LMS GT4
acc:audi_r8_gt4.notes: R8 LMS GT4: the road car's 5.2 NA V10 at about 495 hp with the seven-speed S tronic DCT (auto-data.net, Audi Sport). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Audi R8 LMS GT4, the same car (DCT, synchro-shaped shifts). GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:bmw_m4_gt4.name: BMW M4 GT4
acc:bmw_m4_gt4.notes: The F82 M4 GT4 (2018): S55 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six, about 430 hp by BoP, seven-speed M DCT with race software (BMW Blog, Gooding lot notes). Starting point: the AMS2 BMW M4 GT4 (the later G82 car, S58 with the ZF automatic): same twin-turbo six engine values, shunt carrier at 40 Hz as the other DCT GT4s (AMS2 R8 LMS GT4, 570S GT4). GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:chevrolet_camaro_gt4r.name: Chevrolet Camaro GT4
acc:chevrolet_camaro_gt4r.notes: Camaro GT4.R (2017, Pratt and Miller): dry-sump LT1 6.2 NA pushrod V8, Xtrac six-speed sequential with pneumatic paddle shift, adjustable TC and ABS (Chevrolet launch via NBC Sports, Racer). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Chevrolet Camaro GT4.R, the same car. GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:ginetta_g55_gt4.name: Ginetta G55 GT4
acc:ginetta_g55_gt4.notes: G55 GT4 (2012 homologation): Ford Cyclone 3.7 NA V6, about 370 to 380 hp, Hewland six-speed sequential (Wikipedia, Ginetta G55); TC and ABS added in Ginetta's 2017 upgrade, and the ACC car has both (Endurance-Info 2017, Coach Dave). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Ginetta G55 GT4, the same car. GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:ktm_xbow_gt4.name: KTM X-Bow GT4
acc:ktm_xbow_gt4.notes: X-Bow GT4 (2016): Audi 2.0 TFSI turbo inline-four, about 320 to 360 hp by BoP, Holinger six-speed sequential, Bosch Motorsport ABS and TC (Wikipedia, KTM X-Bow; Hagerty listing of chassis 001). Starting point: the turbo-four GT4 values of the AMS2 Alpine A110 GT4 EVO (sequential box), rock 0.6 from the AC KTM X-Bow R (the same engine bolted rigidly behind the driver). GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:maserati_mc_gt4.name: Maserati MC GT4
acc:maserati_mc_gt4.notes: GranTurismo MC GT4 (the 2016 Trofeo-based car): 4.7 NA V8 (4691 cc), about 430 hp after the GT4 restrictor, six-speed sequential with paddles (Ultimatecarpage, Top Speed). Caution: the 2009 original had a synchromesh paddle box and no ABS (Maserati data via RaceXpress 2009); the 2016 car's ABS is reported only by Lapmeta and its TC is unconfirmed: confirm against the ACC car. Starting point: same values as the AC GranTurismo MC GT4 (ac:ks_maserati_gt_mc_gt4). ABS and TC on.

acc:mclaren_570s_gt4.name: McLaren 570S GT4
acc:mclaren_570s_gt4.notes: 570S GT4: M838TE 3.8 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 restricted to about 450 hp, seven-speed SSG DCT (McLaren). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 McLaren 570S GT4, the same car. GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:mercedes_amg_gt4.name: Mercedes-AMG GT4
acc:mercedes_amg_gt4.notes: AMG GT4: M178 4.0 twin-turbo cross-plane V8, AMG seven-speed DCT transaxle (Mercedes-AMG customer racing). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Mercedes-AMG GT4, the same car. GT4: ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_718_cayman_gt4_mr.name: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4
acc:porsche_718_cayman_gt4_mr.notes: 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport (2019; the id says MR, Manthey Racing): 3.8 NA flat-six at 425 hp, six-speed PDK, rear-drive (Elferspot, PCarMarket listings). Starting point: same values as the AC Cayman GT4 Clubsport (ac:ks_porsche_cayman_gt4_clubsport) and the AMS2 Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR (same 3.8 flat-six and PDK, synchro-shaped). GT4: ABS and TC on, as on the AC and AMS2 Clubsport entries (PSM-derived; not separately confirmed for the 718).

acc:audi_r8_lms_gt2.name: Audi R8 LMS GT2
acc:audi_r8_lms_gt2.notes: R8 LMS GT2 (2019 reveal, ACC 2021 car): 5.2 NA V10 at 640 hp (Audi), seven-speed S tronic DCT taken from the GT4 car (Drive.com.au, Goodwood 2019; the gearbox is from one report). Starting point: V10 engine values of the AC R8 LMS 2016 (GT3-level output), driveline of the AMS2 Audi R8 LMS GT4 (same DCT, synchro-shaped) with shunt 0.6 for the extra torque. GT2: ABS and TC on.

acc:bmw_m2_cs_racing.name: BMW M2 CS Racing
acc:bmw_m2_cs_racing.notes: M2 CS Racing (2020, ACC class TCX): S55 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six, about 280 to 365 hp by BoP, 550 Nm, seven-speed DCT with motorsport software, Drexler LSD; motorsport ABS and DSC standard (BMW M Motorsport via BMW Blog). Starting point: the twin-turbo six values of the AMS2 BMW M4 GT4 at a lower amplitude for the lower output, DCT driveline as the BMW M4 GT4 here, and the BMW cup-car precedent of the AC M235i Racing (ac:ks_bmw_m235i_racing). ABS and TC on.

acc:ferrari_488_challenge_evo.name: Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo
acc:ferrari_488_challenge_evo.notes: 488 Challenge Evo (2020): F154 3.9 twin-turbo flat-plane V8 at 670 hp, seven-speed F1 DCT with race shift maps; Challenge cars keep ABS and F1-Trac TC (Ferrari Corse Clienti). Starting point: same values as the AC 488 Challenge Evo (ac:ks_ferrari_488_challenge_evo), the same car. ABS and TC on.

acc:ktm_xbow_gt2.name: KTM X-Bow GT2
acc:ktm_xbow_gt2.notes: X-Bow GT2 (2021): Audi 2.5 TFSI turbo inline-five developed by Lehmann, up to 600 hp at 7000 rpm, Holinger six-speed sequential with electric shift; Continental racing ABS (ten steps) and adjustable TC (KTM). Starting point: the turbo five values of the AC Audi TT VLN (ac:ks_audi_tt_vln, the same 2.5 five family with a race exhaust and sequential box), driveline at GT3 level with shunt 0.75 for 720 Nm. GT2: ABS and TC on.

acc:lamborghini_huracan_st.name: Lamborghini Huracan SuperTrofeo
acc:lamborghini_huracan_st.notes: Huracan LP 620-2 Super Trofeo (2015): 5.2 NA V10 at 620 hp, rear-drive, Xtrac sequential with a Magneti Marelli electric actuator, Bosch Motorsport ABS and TC adjustable from the wheel (Lamborghini launch release via Supercars.net, Lambocars). Starting point: same values as the AC Huracan ST (ac:ks_lamborghini_huracan_st), the same car. ABS and TC on.

acc:lamborghini_huracan_st_evo2.name: Lamborghini Huracan Super Trofeo EVO2
acc:lamborghini_huracan_st_evo2.notes: Super Trofeo EVO2 (2021): the same 5.2 NA V10 at 620 hp and Xtrac sequential as the first Super Trofeo, with its ABS and TC. Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Super Trofeo (ams2:LamborghiniHuracanLP6202SuperTrofeo, noted there as the EVO2) and the AC Huracan ST. ABS and TC on.

acc:maserati_mc20_gt2.name: Maserati MC20 GT2
acc:maserati_mc20_gt2.notes: MC20 GT2 (2023): Nettuno 3.0 twin-turbo V6 (630 hp base engine before BoP), the road DCT replaced by a six-speed sequential racing box with paddles; adjustable racing ABS and Maserati Corse TC (Maserati GT2 technical specification, GTspirit, Motor1). Starting point: engine from the AMS2 Maserati GT2 Stradale (same Nettuno V6) raised to race level, as the AC GT-R GT3 twin-turbo V6; sequential GT3 driveline. GT2: ABS and TC on.

acc:mercedes_amg_gt2.name: Mercedes-AMG GT2
acc:mercedes_amg_gt2.notes: AMG GT2 (2023): 4.0 twin-turbo V8 with a flat-plane crank, related to the GT Black Series engine, up to 707 hp and 800 Nm, front-mid with a torque tube to an AMG six-speed sequential pneumatic transaxle; multi-adjustable ABS (Mercedes-AMG customer racing, Race Engine Technology, Motor1). Starting point: flat-plane twin-turbo V8 values of the AMS2 McLaren 720S GT3, shunt 0.75 for the torque. GT2: ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_935.name: Porsche 935
acc:porsche_935.notes: The 2019 935 (77 built): the 991.2 GT2 RS Clubsport powertrain, 3.8 twin-turbo flat-six at 700 PS and 750 Nm, seven-speed PDK transaxle (Elferspot listings, Porsche); PSM with ABS and TC from the Clubsport (Porsche newsroom). Starting point: twin-turbo flat-six race values of the AC 911 GT1-98 (ac:ks_porsche_911_gt1) with a smaller lift dump (1.6) for modern turbos; PDK driveline shaped like the AC Cayman GT4 Clubsport (synchro shape) with shunt 0.65 for the torque. ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_991_gt2_rs_mr.name: Porsche 911 GT2 RS Clubsport Evo
acc:porsche_991_gt2_rs_mr.notes: 911 GT2 RS Clubsport with the 2023 Evo kit (Manthey, hence MR in the id): 3.8 twin-turbo flat-six, 515 kW (700 hp) at 7000 rpm, seven-speed PDK; PSM with ABS, TC and ESC, switchable by map (Porsche Motorsport, Porsche newsroom). Starting point: same values as the Porsche 935 here (the same powertrain). ABS and TC on.

acc:porsche_991ii_gt3_cup.name: Porsche 991II GT3 Cup
acc:porsche_991ii_gt3_cup.notes: 991.2 GT3 Cup (2017): 4.0 NA flat-six at 485 PS, six-speed sequential dog box (Porsche Motorsport). Starting point: same values as the AC 911 GT3 Cup 2017 (ac:ks_porsche_911_gt3_cup_2017), the same car. GTC one-make: no ABS, no TC.

acc:porsche_992_gt3_cup.name: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (Type 992)
acc:porsche_992_gt3_cup.notes: 992 GT3 Cup (2021): 4.0 (3996 cc) NA flat-six at 510 PS and 8400 rpm, six-speed sequential dog box; ABS and TC exist only as options stored in the electronics, switched off in the Supercup and most Carrera Cups (Porsche newsroom 2020). Starting point: same values as the AMS2 Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (992), the same car. GTC one-make: no ABS, no TC.

acevo:ks_abarth_695_biposto.name: Abarth 695 Biposto
acevo:ks_abarth_695_biposto.notes: 1.4 T-Jet inline-four turbo, 190 CV, the engine of the 695 Assetto Corse racer with an Akrapovic exhaust (Abarth). Five-speed H-pattern, front-drive; the real car offered a Bacci Romano dog-ring box (gearbox 1 if EVO models it). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: engine from ac:ks_abarth500_assetto_corse (same 190 hp engine and exhaust), softened to a road H-pattern driveline.

acevo:ks_alfa_romeo_giulia_gtam.name: Alfa Romeo Giulia GTAm
acevo:ks_alfa_romeo_giulia_gtam.notes: 2.9 twin-turbo 90-degree V6 at 540 CV, eight-speed ZF automatic, rear-drive (Alfa Romeo). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: ac:ks_alfa_giulia_qv (same engine at 510 hp), a little more of everything for the GTAm's Akrapovic exhaust and lighter body.

acevo:ks_alfa_romeo_junior.name: Alfa Romeo Junior
acevo:ks_alfa_romeo_junior.notes: Junior Elettrica Veloce 280: one front motor, 207 kW (280 CV), single-speed reduction, front Torsen LSD, front-drive (Alfa Romeo). Electric: cylinders 1 and litres 0.1 are the registry minimums, unused by the electric law. Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: no electric entry exists yet; motor whine on the buzz (0.6), no rock, thump, pops or lift-off, no clutch or lug, reduction-gear whine 0.4, tip-in shunt 0.4.

acevo:ks_alpine_a110_s.name: Alpine A110 S
acevo:ks_alpine_a110_s.notes: 1.8 turbo inline-four (M5P) at 300 PS, mid-engined, seven-speed Getrag DCT, rear-drive (Alpine). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: engine from ams2:Alpine A110 GT4 EVO (same 1.8 turbo) toned down for the road exhaust, DCT driveline shaped like the other road DCT cars.

acevo:ks_alpine_a290_b.name: Alpine A290 Beta
acevo:ks_alpine_a290_b.notes: A290 Beta concept: front-drive electric hot hatch on the A290's 160 kW (220 hp) front motor, single-speed (Alpine). Electric: cylinders 1 and litres 0.1 are the registry minimums, unused by the electric law. ABS and ESC. Starting point: same shape as ks_alfa_romeo_junior (no electric entry exists yet), motor whine a touch lower.

acevo:ks_audi_r8_v10_performance.name: Audi R8 V10 performance quattro
acevo:ks_audi_r8_v10_performance.notes: 5.2 V10 NA at 620 PS, seven-speed S tronic, quattro (Audi). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: same values as ac:ks_audi_r8_plus (same engine and box; ams2:Audi R8 V10 GT carries them too).

acevo:ks_audi_rs_3_sportback.name: Audi RS 3 Sportback
acevo:ks_audi_rs_3_sportback.notes: Fourth-generation RS 3: 2.5 TFSI inline-five turbo at 400 PS, seven-speed S tronic, quattro with the torque splitter (Audi). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: engine from ac:ks_audi_tt_vln (same 2.5 five and its 20 Hz warble) with a road exhaust, road DCT driveline.

acevo:ks_audi_rs_6_avant.name: Audi RS 6 Avant
acevo:ks_audi_rs_6_avant.notes: C8 RS 6 Avant: 4.0 TFSI twin-turbo V8 at 600 PS, eight-speed tiptronic, quattro, about 2.1 t (Audi). Road car: ABS and ESC. Starting point: ac:ks_maserati_quattroporte (twin-turbo V8 saloon on an automatic), a bit more rumble and overrun for the RS exhaust.

acevo:ks_bmw_m2_coupe.name: BMW M2 Coupe
acevo:ks_bmw_m2_coupe.notes: G87 M2: S58 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six at 460 PS, six-speed manual (Standard) or eight-speed automatic (Performance variant), rear-drive (BMW). Road car: ABS and DSC. Starting point: ac:ks_bmw_m4 (S55 straight six with the same character), road clutch for the manual.

acevo:ks_bmw_m4_csl.name: BMW M4 CSL
acevo:ks_bmw_m4_csl.notes: G82 M4 CSL: S58 3.0 twin-turbo inline-six at 550 PS, eight-speed M Steptronic, rear-drive (BMW). Road car: ABS and DSC. Starting point: ac:ks_bmw_m4 (straight six of the same family), sharper for the CSL's lighter shell and exhaust.

acevo:ks_bmw_m8_competition.name: BMW M8 Competition
